authors: Pau Ferrer-Cid, Jose M. Barcelo-Ordinas, Jorge Garcia-Vidal, Antonio Avila-Torrado
title: Evaluating missing value imputation strategies to enhance IoT data availability in the edgeAI
validity_discussion: Evaluates VAE, CVAE, MICE, and KNN for missing value imputation in edge computing, focusing on uncertainty quantification (UQ) and confidence intervals. Notes that VAE provides robust 90%-95% UQ coverage and that MICE degrades under MNAR block missingness. Quote: "The results show that the VAE is able to obtain good imputation performances (R2 greater than 0.90) while providing good uncertainty quantification (UQ) estimates with around 90%-95% of samples falling within the estimated confidence intervals."

authors: Christopher Willis, Dylan A. Goodin, Hunter A. Miller, Sally Suliman, Hermann B. Frieboes
title: Evaluation of accuracy and potential biases of imputation methods on biomedical datasets subject to different mechanisms and patterns of missingness
validity_discussion: Critiques individual error metrics (RMSE/NRMSE) for failing to produce valid statistical inference, showing that multiple imputation (MI) methods preserve variance and distribution fidelity (NLWD/coverage) despite higher NRMSE. Quote: "As early as 1996, imputation methods that optimized for minimal error for individual imputed value (e.g., mean square error or absolute error) were criticized for failing to produce 'valid inference'... MI methods prioritize distribution accuracy at the expense of increased imputation error..."

authors: Omar Boursalie, Reza Samavi, Thomas E. Doyle
title: Evaluation methodology for deep learning imputation models
validity_discussion: Distinguishes the goal of statistical imputation (preserving underlying distribution and data variability to avoid inferential bias under Rubin's framework) from deep learning's focus on RMSE minimization, proposing an aggregated Reconstruction Loss metric. Quote: "However, the goal of imputation in the statistical literature is to ensure the imputed data meets the underlying properties of the dataset (e.g. data variability and distribution) rather than achieve the best prediction accuracy as in deep learning."

authors: Luqi He, Yingke Lu, Carl F. Falk, Heungsun Hwang
title: Evaluation of Generative Adversarial Imputation Nets' Performance in Handling Missing Data in Structural Equation Modeling
validity_discussion: Warns that GAIN acts like single imputation, underestimating standard errors and inflating sample size, which invalidates chi-square based fit statistics and increases parameter variability compared to MI and FIML. Quote: "GAIN operates similarly to single imputation by generating a single completed dataset to which a CFA model is fitted. However, single imputation tends to underestimate standard errors and inflate the effective sample size, resulting in inaccurate chi-square statistics... These limitations may undermine the primary goals of missing data techniques—namely, minimizing bias and retaining statistical power..."

authors: Deepa Fernandes Prabhu, Jaeyoung Park, Varadraj P. Gurupur
title: Entropy Guided Benchmarking of Classical and Generative Imputation Methods for High-Dimensional Healthcare Survey Data
validity_discussion: Evaluates classical and deep generative models (VAE, GAN, WGAN, Diffusion) under MCAR/MAR frameworks, noting that simplistic or error-minimized imputation distorts multivariate relationships and compromises statistical validity. Quote: "When missing values are not handled appropriately, they can reduce statistical power, introduce bias, and ultimately compromise the validity and generalizability of both predictive models and inferential analyses... MI remains widely used in epidemiology because it can preserve uncertainty and reduce bias under MAR assumptions..."
